props.title: The Wedding Planner

sections.content: **The Wedding Planner** (2001) arrived at the peak of Jennifer Lopez's rom-com era, following her breakout in **Selena** (1997). The film cemented the "professional woman falls for unavailable man" template that dominated early 2000s romantic comedies. Like **Sweet Home Alabama** (2002) and **Made of Honor** (2008), it plays with the irony of a wedding industry professional experiencing romantic chaos. Matthew McConaughey delivers his signature easygoing charm years before his "McConaissance" dramatic turn in **Dallas Buyers Club** (2013).

sections.content: The film reflects Hollywood's early 2000s fascination with the wedding industry, spawning numerous imitators. **My Best Friend's Wedding** (1997) had already proven the commercial viability of wedding-centered plots, while **Father of the Bride** (1991) demonstrated their family appeal. This wave continued through **Monster-in-Law** (2005) and **The Wedding Date** (2005), capitalizing on audiences' appetite for both romance and wedding spectacle.

The Wedding Planner's success helped establish Jennifer Lopez's rom-com credentials, leading to **Maid in Manhattan** (2002) and **Monster-in-Law** (2005). It also marked a shift from the more grounded 90s romantic comedies like **When Harry Met Sally** (1989) to the profession-focused romantic comedies of the 2000s, where characters' jobs often drove the plot, as seen in **How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days** (2003) and **Two Weeks Notice** (2002). sections.content: The genre evolved beyond simple wedding narratives into more complex explorations of modern relationships. **Bridesmaids** (2011) brought raw comedy and female friendship to the forefront, while **Crazy Rich Asians** (2018) used wedding culture to explore class and cultural differences. These films expanded the wedding movie beyond simple romance into social commentary, though **The Wedding Planner** remains a quintessential example of the classic formula.
